title: $g^*$ is symmetric monoidal
statement:
The strong monoidal functor $g^*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] is compatible
with the symmetries: it is a symmetric monoidal functor. In particular $g^*$ sends
commutative ring objects to commutative ring objects.

proof.text:
Write $L=g^*$, $R=g_*$, $\mathcal C=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ and $\mathcal D=\Sh(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$; these are symmetric monoidal under the hypotheses inherited from [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]. Let $\Phi_{H,K}\colon\Hom(LH,K)\cong\Hom(H,RK)$ be the natural adjunction bijection of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], with unit $\eta_H=\Phi_{H,LH}(\mathrm{id}_{LH})$. Denote the lax tensor map of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal] by $m_{P,Q}\colon RP\otimes RQ\to R(P\otimes Q)$. Unpacking the mate structure specified in [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], put
$$a_{F,G}:=m_{LF,LG}\circ(\eta_F\otimes\eta_G)\colon F\otimes G\longrightarrow R(LF\otimes LG),\qquad \delta_{F,G}:=\Phi_{F\otimes G,LF\otimes LG}^{-1}(a_{F,G}).$$
These $\delta$ are precisely the invertible oplax tensor maps of the specified strong monoidal structure; write $\gamma_{F,G}=\delta_{F,G}^{-1}$ for its lax tensor maps.

proof.text:
Apply the naturality in both variables of the Hom bijection in [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]. The transpose of $\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG}\circ\delta_{F,G}$ is $R(\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG})\circ a_{F,G}$, while the transpose of $\delta_{G,F}\circ L(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G})$ is $a_{G,F}\circ\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G}$. Step 2 identifies these transposes, so injectivity of $\Phi$ gives
$$\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG}\circ\delta_{F,G}=\delta_{G,F}\circ L(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G}).$$
Compose on the left with $\gamma_{G,F}$ and on the right with $\gamma_{F,G}$. The inverse identities for the structure of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] give
$$L(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{F,G})\circ\gamma_{F,G}=\gamma_{G,F}\circ\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LF,LG}.$$
This is the required compatibility of the already strong monoidal functor $L$ with the symmetries.

proof.text:
For a commutative ring object $(B,\rho,e)$ of $\mathcal C$, apply [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], clauses 1 and 2, to the strong monoidal functor $L$ with lax comparison $\gamma$ and lax unit map $j\colon\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D}\to L\mathbf 1_{\mathcal C}$, the inverse of its oplax unit comparison from step 1. Clause 1 gives the ring object $LB$ with multiplication $\rho_L=L(\rho)\circ\gamma_{B,B}$ and unit $e_L=L(e)\circ j\colon\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D}\to LB$. Clause 2 applies because step 3 proves its braided-functor hypothesis. Explicitly,
$$\rho_L\circ\beta^{\mathcal D}_{LB,LB}=L(\rho)\circ L(\beta^{\mathcal C}_{B,B})\circ\gamma_{B,B}=L(\rho\circ\beta^{\mathcal C}_{B,B})\circ\gamma_{B,B}=\rho_L,$$
using $\rho\circ\beta^{\mathcal C}_{B,B}=\rho$. Thus the transported ring object is commutative, including the final clause of the statement.
